entries.text: Your turn stopped mid-way (last note: 'Writing the two example workflows'). Continue from where you are: the working tree has uncommitted action/, docs/ci/ and a pnpm-lock.yaml change. Finish points 3 and 4 of the original task (workflows, actionlint/shellcheck, running the action's steps against a temp copy of <path>, site-builder tests, docs, file:// + static-server check in the preview browser), then verify and commit as instructed and send the full report. One heads-up for the docs: the product direction is shifting toward a hosted service with a local collector; keep the repo-tool path working and documented as is, don't redesign anything for that.

I need to fix actionlint complaints about runner.temp at job-level env by moving CODEX_HOME assignment into a step that writes to GITHUB_ENV instead, and I should check how actionlint handles validating the action.yml file itself versus workflows.



Folded into commit 1. Actionlint flagged that `runner.temp` can't be used in job-level `env` and that it lints workflows rather than `action.yml` directly, so I'll set CODEX_HOME via `$GITHUB_ENV` and lint the action through a workflow that references it as `./action`.

p='docs/ci/agent-ledger.yml'; s=open(p).read()

      BRANCH: agent/run-${{ github.run_id }}'''
assert a in s
s=s.replace(a,'''    env:
      BRANCH: agent/run-${{ github.run_id }}''')
a='''        run: |
          echo "base=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"'''
assert a in s
s=s.replace(a,'''        run: |
          # Job-local Codex home: --match-sessions then sees only this job's sessions.
          export CODEX_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/codex"
          echo "CODEX_HOME=$CODEX_HOME" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "base=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

for f in docs/ci/*.yml; do sed 's#your-org/toolreader/action@main#./action#' $f > $L/.github/workflows/$(basename $f); done

actionlint -shellcheck=$(which shellcheck) docs/ci/*.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml && echo "docs/ci + ci.yml: actionlint clean"

entries.text:
Good, actionlint confirms the real workflows pass against the action while only the intentionally bad one gets flagged. Now I want to test the action's shell steps locally against a fresh temp copy of the demo, trying a tarball-based sync with push to a bare origin, making sure to use a clean copy since the old working directory already has a local agent-ledger.

I'm planning several test scenarios: a fresh origin plus work clone for a sync run with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL unset to emulate CI identity fallback, a site build from a clean clone with no local history, and a directory-mode package test by cloning the repo at HEAD and running pnpm install plus npm pack — this mirrors how `uses:` actually resolves <private> and will take a minute. I also need to rebuild the tarball from current HEAD to make sure it includes the CSS fix, then compare runs using both the directory and tarball package modes.



Actionlint confirmed the broken workflow's errors and showed the real workflows lint clean. Now I'll test the action's script locally against a fresh demo copy — simulating a runner with a bare origin and no git identity — running `sync --push` then `site` from a clean clone.

feat(action): composite GitHub Action for `ledger sync` and `ledger site`

`command: sync | site` with range, codex-home, max-output, push, out and
extra args. It installs toolreader from a tarball, or packs a toolreader
checkout (by default the one the action is in). Runners have no git
identity, so the ledger commit falls back to github-actions[bot]. `site`
takes origin's agent-ledger when the checkout has none and writes
`ledger show` to the job summary. The logic is in run.sh, which reads
INPUT_* variables, so it runs outside Actions too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
docs(ci): example workflows for an agent job and for pull requests

agent-ledger.yml runs `codex exec` with a job-local CODEX_HOME, commits in
a later step and syncs with --match-sessions --push. pr-ledger.yml builds
the page for base..head, uploads it as an artifact and links it in the job
summary; publishing to Pages under pr/<number>/ is opt-in (LEDGER_PAGES),
same-repo PRs only, with the private-repo caveat.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF2
